chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked him about a man who makes the vagina of his female slave permissible (for another man), and he said: 'I do not like that.' There is nothing in it that necessitates the prohibition of what we mentioned, because it came in the place of dislike (karaahah). He explicitly stated this in his saying 'I do not like that.' The reason for the dislike of this is that this is something upon which none of the general public (Sunni scholars) agree with us, and it is something they use to criticize us. Therefore, abstaining from it is superior, even if it is not forbidden. It is also possible that he disliked it only if the freedom of the child was not stipulated; so if that is stipulated, this dislike is removed, which indicates that.

key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ: I do not like (expression of dislike/karaahah)

ai.seo_question: Is making a female slave permissible for another man considered forbidden or merely disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s nuanced stance on *tahil* (making a female slave permissible for another), clarifying that the dislike (*karahah*) is primarily pragmatic rather than juridical. The Imam notes that while the practice is not strictly forbidden, it is disliked because it is a point of contention with the Sunni majority (*al-'ammah*) who criticize it; furthermore, this dislike may be contingent on whether the freedom of the resulting child is stipulated, which would remove the objection.
